entries.shortExplanation: 건조기 means "clothes dryer" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
entries.explanation: 건조기 (geonjogi) means "clothes dryer". Learn it inside a frame, not as a bare word: a useful first chunk is 의류 건조기 ("clothes dryer (full form)"). In Korean the particle or ending next to 건조기 signals its job — topic, subject, object, place, time, method, or description — so read the examples for the small piece beside it. Start with one real sentence about daily routines at home, sleep, doors, windows, and simple requests, then change a single part.

usagePhrases.note: 의류(衣類) = clothing; the full form 의류 건조기 disambiguates from a food dehydrator, but in speech plain 건조기 is enough.
돌리다 (lit. 'spin/turn') is THE verb for any drum appliance — 세탁기 돌리다, 건조기 돌리다. Avoid 켜다 for a full cycle.
Particle 에 marks the destination; 빨래를 건조기에 넣다 = load the laundry into the dryer. Pairs with 꺼내다.
Particle 에서 marks the source you remove from; 꺼내다 (take out) is the natural opposite of 넣다.

examples.ko: 빨래 다 됐으면 건조기에 넣어 줘.
examples.romanization: ppallae da dwaesseumyeon geonjogie neoeo jwo.
examples.en: If the laundry's done, put it in the dryer.
examples.note: Teaches 다 되다 = 'to be finished/ready' (here, done washing); casual 줘 fits a roommate or partner.

examples.ko: 우리 집은 건조기가 없어서 빨래를 베란다에 널어요.
examples.romanization: uri jibeun geonjogiga eopseoseo ppallaereul berandae neoreoyo.
examples.en: We don't have a dryer, so we hang the laundry on the balcony.
examples.note: Teaches 널다 = 'hang out to dry,' the verb used instead of a dryer; 없어서 = 'because there isn't.'

examples.ko: 요즘 건조기는 옷감 안 상하게 저온으로 말려 줘서 인기가 많아요.
examples.romanization: yojeum geonjogineun otgam an sanghage jeooneuro mallyeo jwoseo ingiga manayo.
examples.en: These days dryers are popular because they dry on low heat so the fabric doesn't get damaged.
examples.note: Real selling-point register: 옷감(이) 상하다 = fabric gets ruined; 저온으로 말리다 = dry at low temperature.

entries.nuance: 건조기 = 乾燥機 ('dry-burn machine'), the 機 that 말리다(dries) things. 한국에서는 비교적 최근에야 보편화된 가전이라 아직 없는 집도 많아서, '건조기 있어요?'는 자취방·월세 집을 구할 때 실제로 자주 묻는 질문이에요. 비슷해 보이는 단어로 드라이기(머리 말리는 헤어드라이어)와 식품 건조기가 있는데, 일상 대화의 '건조기'는 거의 항상 의류 건조기를 뜻합니다. 영어 화자가 잘 빠지는 함정은 동사 선택이에요. 영어 'turn on the dryer'를 직역해 '건조기 켜다'라고 하면 전원만 넣은 느낌이라 어색하고, 한 통(load)을 돌려 말린다는 뜻은 반드시 '건조기 돌리다'로 표현합니다. 또 hair dryer를 '건조기'라고 부르면 큰 가전을 떠올리니 머리는 '드라이기'로 구분하세요.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Calling a hair dryer 건조기 — 건조기 is the big standing appliance for clothes; a hair dryer is 드라이기 (or 헤어드라이어). The two are not interchangeable.
Saying 건조기 켜다 for running a load — 켜다 only means 'flip the power on.' For drying a full load Koreans say 건조기 돌리다.
Treating 건조기 as automatically present in any home — in Korea it's a relatively new, often-absent appliance, so '건조기 있어요?' is a genuine question, not small talk.

structuredNuance.t: 옷을 말리는 큰 가전. 한국에서는 비교적 최근에야 보편화된 가전이라 아직 없는 집도 많아서, '건조기 있어요?'는 자취방·월세 집을 구할 때 실제로 자주 묻는 질문이에요.
건조기 = 乾燥機 ('dry-burn machine'), the 機 that 말리다(dries) things.
비슷해 보이는 단어로 드라이기(머리 말리는 헤어드라이어)와 식품 건조기가 있는데, 일상 대화의 '건조기'는 거의 항상 의류 건조기를 뜻합니다. hair dryer를 '건조기'라고 부르면 큰 가전을 떠올리니 머리는 '드라이기'로 구분하세요.
영어 화자가 잘 빠지는 함정은 동사 선택이에요. 영어 'turn on the dryer'를 직역해 '건조기 켜다'라고 하면 전원만 넣은 느낌이라 어색하고, 한 통(load)을 돌려 말린다는 뜻은 반드시 '건조기 돌리다'로 표현합니다.

entries.shortExplanation: 가습기 means "humidifier" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
entries.explanation: "humidifier" is 가습기 (gaseupgi). The word itself is easy; what matters is the company it keeps, like 가습기 틀다 ("turn on the humidifier"). Watch the particle attached to 가습기 in each example — that little marker, not the word, tells you whether it is the topic, the subject, the object, or a place. Copy one full sentence about daily routines at home, sleep, doors, windows, and simple requests first, then vary one word.

usagePhrases.note: 틀다 is the go-to verb for devices that put out air/water/sound (가습기, 에어컨, 선풍기, 음악). More idiomatic here than 켜다.
물(을) 채우다 = fill with water; 채우다 (to fill) is the daily upkeep verb. Opposite of 비우다 (empty).
세척(洗滌) = washing/cleaning; 가습기 세척 is stressed heavily in Korea for hygiene reasons.
살균제(殺菌劑) = germ-killing agent; the word carries a heavy historical association in Korea (see nuance).

examples.en: It's so dry in winter that I sleep with the humidifier on.
examples.note: Teaches 건조하다 = 'to be dry' (air/skin), a stock winter complaint; 틀고 자다 = sleep with (it) on.

examples.ko: 가습기 물 좀 채워 줄래? 거의 다 떨어졌어.
examples.romanization: gaseupgi mul jom chaewo jullae? geoui da tteoreojyeosseo.
examples.en: Can you refill the humidifier? It's almost empty.
examples.note: Teaches 물이 떨어지다 = 'run out of water'; 줄래? is a soft casual request to a peer.

examples.ko: 가습기는 매일 안 씻으면 안에 물때하고 세균이 금방 껴요.
examples.romanization: gaseupgineun maeil an ssiseumyeon ane multtaehago segyuni geumbang kkyeoyo.
examples.en: If you don't wash the humidifier every day, scale and bacteria build up inside fast.
examples.note: Real-situation hygiene register: 물때(가) 끼다 = limescale builds up; reflects post-scandal caution.

entries.nuance: 가습기 = 加濕器, literally '加(add)-濕(moisture)-器(device)' — a device that ADDS humidity, the exact mirror image of 제습기(除濕器), which REMOVES it. 한국 아파트는 겨울 난방이 강해 공기가 매우 건조해지기 때문에 가습기가 거의 필수품이에요. 가장 큰 함정은 정반대 단어인 제습기와의 혼동입니다. 두 단어는 가운데 글자 加(더하다)와 除(없애다)만 다르니, 겨울엔 가습기(촉촉하게), 장마철엔 제습기(뽀송하게)로 외워 두세요. 동사도 주의: 영어 'turn on'을 그대로 '켜다'로 써도 틀리진 않지만, 물·바람을 내보내는 기기에는 '틀다'가 훨씬 자연스럽습니다. 끝으로 '가습기 살균제'는 과거 대규모 인명 피해를 낸 사건과 직결된 무거운 단어라, 한국인은 가습기 청결과 세척에 유난히 민감하다는 문화적 배경도 알아 두면 좋습니다.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Confusing 가습기 (adds moisture, 加濕) with 제습기 (removes moisture, 除濕) — they are exact opposites. Use 가습기 in dry winter, 제습기 in humid summer/rainy season.
Saying 가습기 켜다 — not wrong, but 가습기 틀다 is the natural collocation because it puts out water vapor, like 에어컨/선풍기 틀다.
Mentioning 가습기 살균제 lightly — in Korea this phrase recalls a deadly disinfectant disaster, so it is sensitive, not casual product talk.

structuredNuance.t: 공기에 습기를 더하는 기기. 한국 아파트는 겨울 난방이 강해 공기가 매우 건조해지기 때문에 가습기가 거의 필수품이에요. 끝으로 '가습기 살균제'는 과거 대규모 인명 피해를 낸 사건과 직결된 무거운 단어라, 한국인은 가습기 청결과 세척에 유난히 민감하다는 문화적 배경도 알아 두면 좋습니다.
가습기 = 加濕器, literally '加(add)-濕(moisture)-器(device)' — a device that ADDS humidity, the exact mirror image of 제습기(除濕器), which REMOVES it.
가장 큰 함정은 정반대 단어인 제습기와의 혼동입니다. 두 단어는 가운데 글자 加(더하다)와 除(없애다)만 다르니, 겨울엔 가습기(촉촉하게), 장마철엔 제습기(뽀송하게)로 외워 두세요.
동사도 주의: 영어 'turn on'을 그대로 '켜다'로 써도 틀리진 않지만, 물·바람을 내보내는 기기에는 '틀다'가 훨씬 자연스럽습니다.

entries.shortExplanation: 공기청정기 means "air purifier" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
entries.explanation: 공기청정기 (gonggicheongjeonggi) = "air purifier". Treat it as a building block that needs a frame: 공기청정기 틀다 ("turn on the air purifier") shows how it actually behaves. The grammar lives in the particle or ending beside 공기청정기, so notice that piece as you read, not just the dictionary meaning. Begin from a complete sentence about daily routines at home, sleep, doors, windows, and simple requests and swap just one element to make it yours.

usagePhrases.note: 틀다 for an air-output device; 켜다 is also acceptable here. Casual short form: 공청기.
필터(를) 갈다 = replace the filter; 갈다 = swap out a consumable part (filters, batteries, blades).
미세먼지(微細-) = fine particulate dust; 심하다 = severe. The usual trigger for running the purifier.
돌리다 works too because a fan spins inside; 하루 종일 공기청정기 돌리다 = run it all day.

examples.ko: 미세먼지 심한 날엔 공기청정기를 하루 종일 틀어 놔요.
examples.romanization: misemeonji simhan naren gonggicheongjeonggireul haru jongil teureo nwayo.
examples.en: On days with bad fine dust, I leave the air purifier on all day.
examples.note: Teaches 틀어 놓다 = 'leave (it) turned on'; 하루 종일 = all day long.

examples.ko: 공기청정기 필터 갈 때 됐나 봐. 빨간불 들어왔어.
examples.romanization: gonggicheongjeonggi pilteo gal ttae dwaenna bwa. ppalganbul deureowasseo.
examples.en: Looks like it's time to change the filter. The red light came on.
examples.note: Teaches 빨간불(이) 들어오다 = 'the red light comes on'; ~ㄹ 때 되다 = 'time to do.'

examples.ko: 요즘은 미세먼지 농도 보고 자동으로 세기 조절되는 공기청정기가 많아요.
examples.romanization: yojeumeun misemeonji nongdo bogo jadongeuro segi jojeoldoeneun gonggicheongjeonggiga manayo.
examples.en: These days many purifiers auto-adjust their fan speed based on the dust level.
examples.note: Real product register: 농도 = concentration; 세기(가) 조절되다 = the strength is regulated automatically.

entries.nuance: 공기청정기 = 空氣(air)+淸淨(clean/purify)+器(device): the 器 that 淸淨하게(makes clean) the 空氣(air). 한국은 봄철 미세먼지·황사가 심해 공기청정기가 거의 생활필수품이 됐고, 자취하는 20-30대도 작은 모델 하나쯤 둡니다. 가장 흔한 혼동은 정수기(淨水器)와의 짝꿍 오류예요. 둘 다 '淸/淨'으로 깨끗하게 한다는 뜻이라 헷갈리지만, 공기청정기는 空氣(공기)를, 정수기는 水(물)를 다룹니다 — '청정/정수'의 글자 순서가 다른 것도 단서예요. 또 영어 화자는 'purifier'를 막연히 '청정기'라고만 부르기 쉬운데, 그러면 공기인지 물인지 모호하니 반드시 '공기'를 붙여 공기청정기(또는 캐주얼하게 공청기)라고 해야 통합니다. 동사는 공기를 내보낸다는 점에서 '틀다/돌리다'가 자연스럽고, 켜다도 무방합니다.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Saying just 청정기 — it's ambiguous. Say 공기청정기 (or casual 공청기) so it's clear you mean an AIR purifier, not a water one.
Confusing 공기청정기 (air, 淸淨) with 정수기 (water, 淨水) — the 淸/淨 'clean' element overlaps, but one cleans air and the other cleans water.
Forgetting filter upkeep vocabulary — when the indicator turns red you say 필터 갈 때 됐다 (time to change the filter), using 갈다, not 바꾸다 for a routine consumable.

structuredNuance.t: 공기를 깨끗하게 거르는 기기. 한국은 봄철 미세먼지·황사가 심해 공기청정기가 거의 생활필수품이 됐고, 자취하는 20-30대도 작은 모델 하나쯤 둡니다. 동사는 공기를 내보낸다는 점에서 '틀다/돌리다'가 자연스럽고, 켜다도 무방합니다.
공기청정기 = 空氣(air)+淸淨(clean/purify)+器(device): the 器 that 淸淨하게(makes clean) the 空氣(air).
가장 흔한 혼동은 정수기(淨水器)와의 짝꿍 오류예요. 둘 다 '淸/淨'으로 깨끗하게 한다는 뜻이라 헷갈리지만, 공기청정기는 空氣(공기)를, 정수기는 水(물)를 다룹니다 — '청정/정수'의 글자 순서가 다른 것도 단서예요.
영어 화자는 'purifier'를 막연히 '청정기'라고만 부르기 쉬운데, 그러면 공기인지 물인지 모호하니 반드시 '공기'를 붙여 공기청정기(또는 캐주얼하게 공청기)라고 해야 통합니다.

entries.shortExplanation: 정수기 means "water purifier / water dispenser" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
entries.explanation: 정수기 (jeongsugi) means "water purifier / water dispenser". Learn it inside a frame, not as a bare word: a useful first chunk is 정수기 렌탈 ("water purifier rental"). In Korean the particle or ending next to 정수기 signals its job — topic, subject, object, place, time, method, or description — so read the examples for the small piece beside it. Start with one real sentence about daily routines at home, sleep, doors, windows, and simple requests, then change a single part.

usagePhrases.note: 렌탈(rental) is a huge market in Korea — many rent a 정수기 with a monthly fee rather than buying it outright.
온수(溫水) = hot water; 물(을) 받다 = dispense water into a cup. You 받다 from a dispenser, not 따르다.
냉수(冷水) = cold water; pairs with 온수. You select by pressing the matching button.
코디 = the rental brand's visiting maintenance rep (a Korea-specific term); 방문 = a visit to change filters.

examples.ko: 정수기에서 온수 받아서 컵라면 끓여 먹었어.
examples.romanization: jeongsugieseo onsu badaseo keomnamyeon kkeuryeo meogeosseo.
examples.en: I got hot water from the purifier and made a cup ramyeon.
examples.note: Teaches 물(을) 받다 = 'dispense water into a container'; 에서 marks the source.

examples.ko: 우리 회사 정수기는 냉수가 진짜 시원해요.
examples.romanization: uri hoesa jeongsugineun naengsuga jinjja siwonhaeyo.
examples.en: The water purifier at my office has really cold water.
examples.note: Office 정수기 are standard; teaches 시원하다 = 'refreshingly cold' for water.

examples.ko: 정수기는 사는 사람보다 렌탈해서 코디한테 필터 관리 받는 사람이 더 많아요.
examples.romanization: jeongsugineun saneun saramboda rentalhaeseo kodihante pilteo gwalli banneun sarami deo manayo.
examples.en: More people rent a purifier and get filter service from a rep than buy one outright.
examples.note: Real cultural register: contrasts 사다 vs 렌탈하다; 관리(를) 받다 = receive maintenance.

entries.nuance: 정수기 = 淨水器, '淨(clean)-水(water)-器(device)' — the device that purifies tap water and dispenses 온수(溫水, hot)·냉수(冷水, cold)·정수(淨水, room-temp filtered). 한국 특유의 포인트는 '사는' 것보다 '렌탈'하는 문화예요. 코웨이·SK매직 같은 회사에 매달 요금을 내고 '코디'라는 방문 직원에게 필터 관리를 받죠 — 외국인에게는 이 렌탈 개념이 가장 낯섭니다. 어휘 함정 두 가지: 첫째, 공기청정기(空氣淸淨器)와 글자가 겹쳐(淨/淸) 헷갈리지만 정수기는 물(水), 공기청정기는 공기(空氣)를 다룹니다. 둘째, '정수기 물'은 수돗물을 걸러 마시는 물이고, '생수'는 페트병에 든 사 먹는 물이라 서로 다른 출처예요. 또 컵에 물을 담을 때 영어 'pour' 감각으로 '따르다'를 쓰기 쉬운데, 디스펜서에서는 '물 받다'가 맞습니다.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Mixing up 정수기 (water, 淨水) with 공기청정기 (air, 淸淨) — the shared 淨/淸 'purify' character makes them look similar, but one handles water and the other air.
Saying 물 따르다 for the dispenser — 따르다 is pouring from a kettle/bottle; from a 정수기 you say 물 받다 (catch/receive water into a cup).
Equating 정수기 물 with 생수 — 정수기 물 is filtered tap water from the machine, while 생수 is store-bought bottled water; they are different sources.

structuredNuance.t: 수돗물을 걸러 온수(溫水, hot)·냉수(冷水, cold)·정수(淨水, room-temp filtered)를 내주는 기기. 한국 특유의 포인트는 '사는' 것보다 '렌탈'하는 문화예요. 코웨이·SK매직 같은 회사에 매달 요금을 내고 '코디'라는 방문 직원에게 필터 관리를 받죠 — 외국인에게는 이 렌탈 개념이 가장 낯섭니다.
정수기 = 淨水器, '淨(clean)-水(water)-器(device)' — the device that purifies tap water.
공기청정기(空氣淸淨器)와 글자가 겹쳐(淨/淸) 헷갈리지만 정수기는 물(水), 공기청정기는 공기(空氣)를 다룹니다. 또 '정수기 물'은 수돗물을 걸러 마시는 물이고, '생수'는 페트병에 든 사 먹는 물이라 서로 다른 출처예요.
컵에 물을 담을 때 영어 'pour' 감각으로 '따르다'를 쓰기 쉬운데, 디스펜서에서는 '물 받다'가 맞습니다.

entries.shortExplanation: 식기세척기 means "dishwasher" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
entries.explanation: "dishwasher" is 식기세척기 (sikgisecheokgi). The word itself is easy; what matters is the company it keeps, like 식기세척기 돌리다 ("run the dishwasher"). Watch the particle attached to 식기세척기 in each example — that little marker, not the word, tells you whether it is the topic, the subject, the object, or a place. Copy one full sentence about daily routines at home, sleep, doors, windows, and simple requests first, then vary one word.

usagePhrases.note: 돌리다 for a wash cycle, exactly as with 세탁기/건조기. Casual short form of the noun: 식세기.
설거지(를) 하다 = wash dishes by hand — the chore the machine replaces. Native Korean word, no hanja.
전용(專用) = exclusive-use; 식기세척기 전용 세제 is required — regular dish soap foams over.
그릇(을) 넣다 = put the dishes in; scrape off scraps (음식물 털어 내다) before loading.

examples.ko: 식세기 산 뒤로 설거지 스트레스가 확 줄었어요.
examples.romanization: siksegi san dwiro seolgeoji seuteureseuga hwak jureosseoyo.
examples.en: Ever since I got a dishwasher, my stress over dishes dropped a lot.
examples.note: Casual 식세기; teaches 산 뒤로 = 'ever since buying' (clearer than 사고 나서, which collides with 사고 'accident'); 확 = sharply.

examples.ko: 그릇 식기세척기에 넣기 전에 음식물은 좀 털어 내.
examples.romanization: geureut sikgisecheokgie neoki jeone eumsingmureun jom teoreo nae.
examples.en: Scrape off the food bits before putting the dishes in the dishwasher.
examples.note: Teaches 털어 내다 = 'shake/scrape off'; casual command ~내 ending.

examples.ko: 식기세척기에는 일반 주방세제 말고 꼭 전용 세제를 써야 돼요.
examples.romanization: sikgisecheokgieneun ilban jubangseje malgo kkok jeonyong sejereul sseoya dwaeyo.
examples.en: In a dishwasher you must use dedicated detergent, not regular dish soap.
examples.note: Real warning register: A 말고 B = 'B, not A'; 꼭 ~야 되다 = 'absolutely must.'

entries.nuance: 식기세척기 = 食器(tableware)+洗滌(washing)+機(machine): the 機 that 洗滌(washes) the 食器(dishes). 줄여서 '식세기'라고도 부르고, 한국 신혼부부와 1인 가구 사이에서 인기가 빠르게 느는 가전이에요. 가장 흔한 철자 함정은 세탁기(洗濯機)에 이끌려 '식기세탁기'라고 쓰는 것 — 그릇은 '濯(빨다, 헹구다)'이 아니라 '滌(씻다)'을 써서 식기세척'기'가 맞습니다(세탁이 아니라 세척). 두 번째 함정은 세제예요. 영어권에서 dish soap 한 가지만 떠올리기 쉬운데, 한국에서는 손 설거지용 '주방세제'와 기계용 '식기세척기 전용 세제'가 따로이고, 일반 주방세제를 넣으면 거품이 넘쳐 고장 납니다. 동사는 한 사이클 돌린다는 뜻으로 '돌리다'를 쓰며, 손 설거지(설거지하다)와 대비해 기억하면 좋습니다.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Writing 식기세탁기 by analogy with 세탁기 — the correct word is 식기세척기. Laundry uses 세탁(洗濯); dishes use 세척(洗滌).
Using regular 주방세제 (hand dish soap) in the machine — only 식기세척기 전용 세제 works; ordinary soap produces too many suds and can damage it.
Saying 식기세척기 켜다 for a wash — like other drum appliances it takes 돌리다 (식기세척기 돌리다 = run a cycle).

structuredNuance.t: 그릇을 자동으로 씻는 가전. 줄여서 '식세기'라고도 부르고, 한국 신혼부부와 1인 가구 사이에서 인기가 빠르게 느는 가전이에요. 동사는 한 사이클 돌린다는 뜻으로 '돌리다'를 쓰며, 손 설거지(설거지하다)와 대비해 기억하면 좋습니다.
식기세척기 = 食器(tableware)+洗滌(washing)+機(machine): the 機 that 洗滌(washes) the 食器(dishes).

가장 흔한 철자 함정은 세탁기(洗濯機)에 이끌려 '식기세탁기'라고 쓰는 것 — 그릇은 '濯(빨다, 헹구다)'이 아니라 '滌(씻다)'을 써서 식기세척'기'가 맞습니다(세탁이 아니라 세척). 두 번째 함정은 세제예요. 영어권에서 dish soap 한 가지만 떠올리기 쉬운데, 한국에서는 손 설거지용 '주방세제'와 기계용 '식기세척기 전용 세제'가 따로이고, 일반 주방세제를 넣으면 거품이 넘쳐 고장 납니다.

entries.shortExplanation: 인덕션 means "induction cooktop" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
entries.explanation: 인덕션 (indeoksyeon) = "induction cooktop". Treat it as a building block that needs a frame: 인덕션 전용 냄비 ("induction-compatible pot") shows how it actually behaves. The grammar lives in the particle or ending beside 인덕션, so notice that piece as you read, not just the dictionary meaning. Begin from a complete sentence about daily routines at home, sleep, doors, windows, and simple requests and swap just one element to make it yours.

usagePhrases.note: 전용(專用) = exclusive-use; you need a magnetic (ferrous) bottom or the pot won't heat at all.
불(을) 조절하다 = control the heat; Koreans still say 불 ('fire') on induction out of habit, though there's no flame.
닦다 = wipe; its flat glass surface is a selling point — 닦기 편하다 (easy to clean).
The older alternative; people compare 인덕션 vs 가스레인지 when moving into a new place.

examples.ko: 요즘 원룸은 가스 대신 인덕션이 많아요.
examples.romanization: yojeum wollumeun gaseu daesin indeoksyeoni manayo.
examples.en: These days a lot of studio apartments have induction instead of gas.
examples.note: Teaches 원룸 = one-room studio; A 대신 B = 'B instead of A,' a real new-build trend.

examples.ko: 인덕션은 냄비를 아무거나 못 써. 전용이어야 돼.
examples.romanization: indeoksyeoneun naembireul amugeona mot sseo. jeonyongieoya dwae.
examples.en: You can't use just any pot on induction. It has to be the compatible kind.
examples.note: Teaches 아무거나 + 못 + verb = 'can't use just anything'; ~이어야 되다 = 'has to be.'

examples.ko: 냄비 바닥에 자석 붙으면 인덕션에서 쓸 수 있어요.
examples.romanization: naembi badage jaseok buteumyeon indeoksyeoneseo sseul su isseoyo.
examples.en: If a magnet sticks to the pot's bottom, you can use it on induction.
examples.note: Real practical test: 자석(이) 붙다 = a magnet sticks; the everyday way Koreans check induction compatibility.

entries.nuance: 인덕션은 영어 'induction'을 그대로 들여온 외래어로, 자기장으로 냄비 바닥을 직접 가열하는 전기 인덕션 레인지를 가리켜요(한자어가 아닙니다). 화재 위험이 적고 평평한 유리 상판이라 닦기 쉬워서 한국 신축 아파트·원룸의 기본 옵션이 되고 있죠. 가장 큰 함정은 냄비예요. 자석이 붙는 '인덕션 전용'(바닥에 철 성분) 냄비라야 작동해서, 이사 후 기존 유리·알루미늄 냄비를 못 쓰는 일이 흔합니다 — 그래서 '냄비 바닥에 자석 붙나?'로 확인하는 게 생활 팁이에요. 또 비슷한 전기 상판인 '하이라이트(전기레인지)'와 헷갈리기 쉬운데, 하이라이트는 열선으로 데워 어떤 냄비든 되지만 인덕션은 자성 냄비만 됩니다. 불꽃이 없어도 한국인은 세기 조절을 여전히 '불 조절'이라고 말한다는 점도 알아 두세요.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Assuming any pot works — only cookware with a magnetic (ferrous) base heats on 인덕션. Test with a fridge magnet or look for the 인덕션 전용 mark.
Confusing 인덕션 with 하이라이트/전기레인지 (radiant electric) — they look alike, but 하이라이트 heats any pot via a coil, while 인덕션 needs magnetic cookware.
Avoiding 불 because there's no flame — Koreans still say 불 조절 (adjust the 'fire') on induction; switching to a literal word sounds unnatural.

structuredNuance.t: 자기장으로 냄비 바닥을 직접 가열하는 전기 인덕션 레인지. 화재 위험이 적고 평평한 유리 상판이라 닦기 쉬워서 한국 신축 아파트·원룸의 기본 옵션이 되고 있죠. 불꽃이 없어도 한국인은 세기 조절을 여전히 '불 조절'이라고 말한다는 점도 알아 두세요.
인덕션은 영어 'induction'을 그대로 들여온 외래어예요(한자어가 아닙니다).
비슷한 전기 상판인 '하이라이트(전기레인지)'와 헷갈리기 쉬운데, 하이라이트는 열선으로 데워 어떤 냄비든 되지만 인덕션은 자성 냄비만 됩니다.
가장 큰 함정은 냄비예요. 자석이 붙는 '인덕션 전용'(바닥에 철 성분) 냄비라야 작동해서, 이사 후 기존 유리·알루미늄 냄비를 못 쓰는 일이 흔합니다 — 그래서 '냄비 바닥에 자석 붙나?'로 확인하는 게 생활 팁이에요.

entries.shortExplanation: 전기장판 means "electric heating pad / electric blanket" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
entries.explanation: 전기장판 (jeongijangpan) means "electric heating pad / electric blanket". Learn it inside a frame, not as a bare word: a useful first chunk is 전기장판 켜다 ("turn on the electric pad"). In Korean the particle or ending next to 전기장판 signals its job — topic, subject, object, place, time, method, or description — so read the examples for the small piece beside it. Start with one real sentence about daily routines at home, sleep, doors, windows, and simple requests, then change a single part.

usagePhrases.note: 켜다 fits a simple on/off device with a switch or dial — unlike air/water appliances, here 틀다 is less common.
온도(溫度)(를) 조절하다 = set the temperature on its dial controller; 약하게/세게 = low/high.
저온(低溫) 화상 = a burn from prolonged contact with mild heat; the standard safety warning for these pads.
온수매트 = a mat that circulates warm water instead of using a coil; marketed as a safer alternative.

examples.ko: 보일러 틀기 아까워서 전기장판만 켜고 자.
examples.romanization: boilleo teulgi akkawoseo jeongijangpanman kyeogo ja.
examples.en: Running the heating feels wasteful, so I just sleep with the electric pad on.
examples.note: Teaches 아깝다 = 'feel reluctant to spend/waste'; ~만 켜다 = turn on just that, a relatable money-saver.

examples.ko: 전기장판 너무 뜨겁게 틀고 자면 저온 화상 입을 수 있어요.
examples.romanization: jeongijangpan neomu tteugeopge teulgo jamyeon jeoon hwasang ibeul su isseoyo.
examples.en: If you sleep with the electric pad turned up too high, you can get a low-temperature burn.
examples.note: Teaches 화상(을) 입다 = 'get burned'; a real safety caution about cranking the heat overnight.

examples.ko: 겨울엔 전기장판 위에 이불 깔고 귤 까먹으면서 뒹굴뒹굴해요.
examples.romanization: gyeouren jeongijangpan wie ibul kkalgo gyul kkameogeumyeonseo dwingguldwinggulhaeyo.
examples.en: In winter I lay a blanket on the electric pad, peel tangerines, and just laze around.
examples.note: Cozy real-life image: 깔다 = spread/lay down; 뒹굴뒹굴하다 = roll around/lounge, very Korean winter vibe.

entries.nuance: 전기장판 = 電氣(electric) + 장판(壯版, originally the oiled-paper floor covering Koreans sat on) — so it literally means an 'electric floor mat' you heat and lie on. 한국 겨울의 대표적인 가성비 난방템이에요. 가스보일러를 돌리면 가스비가 많이 나오니, 자취생이나 절약하는 사람은 방 전체 대신 몸만 따뜻하게 데우려고 전기장판을 켜죠. 어휘 구분 두 가지: 첫째, 열선으로 데우는 '전기장판'과 따뜻한 물을 순환시키는 '온수매트'는 다른 제품으로, 후자가 더 안전하다고 광고됩니다. 둘째, 동사 선택 — 물·바람을 내보내는 가습기·에어컨엔 '틀다'가 자연스럽지만, 단순 전원식인 전기장판엔 '켜다'가 가장 무난합니다(틀다도 쓰이긴 함). 영어 화자가 놓치기 쉬운 점은 안전 경고예요. 열이 미지근해 안전해 보여도 밤새 켜 두면 '저온 화상'을 입을 수 있으니, 따뜻함을 가볍게 여기지 말라는 주의가 늘 따라붙습니다.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Treating mild warmth as harmless — sleeping on it all night on high can cause 저온 화상 (a low-temperature burn). Korean advice always pairs the pad with this caution.
Confusing 전기장판 (electric coil mat) with 온수매트 (circulating hot-water mat) — they're different products; the water mat is marketed as safer and burn-free.
Over-using 틀다 from other appliances — for this simple on/off heater, 전기장판 켜다 is the natural verb, not 틀다.

structuredNuance.t: 열선으로 데워 그 위에 누워 자는 전기 바닥 매트. 한국 겨울의 대표적인 가성비 난방템이에요. 가스보일러를 돌리면 가스비가 많이 나오니, 자취생이나 절약하는 사람은 방 전체 대신 몸만 따뜻하게 데우려고 전기장판을 켜죠.
전기장판 = 電氣(electric) + 장판(壯版, originally the oiled-paper floor covering Koreans sat on) — so it literally means an 'electric floor mat' you heat and lie on.
열선으로 데우는 '전기장판'과 따뜻한 물을 순환시키는 '온수매트'는 다른 제품으로, 후자가 더 안전하다고 광고됩니다.
동사 선택 — 물·바람을 내보내는 가습기·에어컨엔 '틀다'가 자연스럽지만, 단순 전원식인 전기장판엔 '켜다'가 가장 무난합니다(틀다도 쓰이긴 함). 또 열이 미지근해 안전해 보여도 밤새 켜 두면 '저온 화상'을 입을 수 있으니, 따뜻함을 가볍게 여기지 말라는 주의가 늘 따라붙습니다.

entries.shortExplanation: 제습기 means "dehumidifier" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
entries.explanation: "dehumidifier" is 제습기 (jeseupgi). The word itself is easy; what matters is the company it keeps, like 제습기 돌리다 ("run the dehumidifier"). Watch the particle attached to 제습기 in each example — that little marker, not the word, tells you whether it is the topic, the subject, the object, or a place. Copy one full sentence about daily routines at home, sleep, doors, windows, and simple requests first, then vary one word.

usagePhrases.note: 돌리다 is common because a compressor/fan runs inside; 틀다 also fine. Avoid 켜다 for a long session.
물통(을) 비우다 = empty the collected-water tank, the main upkeep task. Opposite of 채우다.
습(濕)하다 = muggy/damp — the air condition that makes you reach for the 제습기.
곰팡이(가) 피다/슬다 = mold grows; preventing 곰팡이 is a top reason to run a dehumidifier.

examples.ko: 장마철엔 집이 너무 습해서 제습기를 계속 돌려요.
examples.romanization: jangmacheoren jibi neomu seupaeseo jeseupgireul gyesok dollyeoyo.
examples.en: During the rainy season the house gets so damp that I keep the dehumidifier running.
examples.note: Teaches 장마철 = rainy season; 습하다 = humid/damp; 계속 돌리다 = keep it running.

examples.ko: 제습기 물통 꽉 찼어. 비워야 돼.
examples.romanization: jeseupgi multong kkwak chasseo. biwoya dwae.
examples.en: The dehumidifier's tank is full. It needs emptying.
examples.note: Teaches 꽉 차다 = 'be completely full'; 비우다 = empty (opposite of 채우다).

examples.ko: 건조기 없어서 비 오는 날엔 제습기 틀어 놓고 빨래 말려요.
examples.romanization: geonjogi eopseoseo bi oneun naren jeseupgi teureo noko ppallae mallyeoyo.
examples.en: Without a dryer, on rainy days I run the dehumidifier and dry the laundry with it.
examples.note: Real workaround register: a dehumidifier doubles as a laundry dryer; 틀어 놓다 = leave running.

entries.nuance: 제습기 = 除濕器, '除(remove)-濕(moisture)-器(device)' — it pulls dampness OUT of the air, the exact opposite of 가습기(加濕器), which adds it. 한국 여름은 장마와 높은 습도 때문에 제습기 수요가 급증하고, 곰팡이 예방과 실내 건조에 쓰이며, 건조기가 없는 집에서는 빨래 말리는 용도로도 자주 씁니다. 가장 큰 함정은 역시 가습기와의 혼동이에요. 가운데 글자 除(없애다)와 加(더하다)만 다르니, '여름·장마=제습기(뽀송), 겨울=가습기(촉촉)'로 묶어 외우면 안전합니다. 두 번째 함정은 물통 관리예요. 모은 물이 가득 차면 안전을 위해 자동으로 멈추는데, 이를 모르는 초보자는 고장으로 오해하기 쉽습니다 — 사실은 '물통(을) 비우다'를 해 주면 다시 돌아갑니다. 동사는 '돌리다/틀다'가 자연스럽습니다.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Confusing 제습기 (removes moisture, 除濕) with 가습기 (adds moisture, 加濕) — only the middle character (除 'remove' vs 加 'add') differs, but the function flips entirely.
Thinking it broke when it stops — a full 물통 makes it auto-stop for safety. Beginners read this as a malfunction; you just need to 물통 비우다 (empty the tank).
Forgetting it can dry laundry — in homes without a 건조기, running the 제습기 in the room is a normal way to dry clothes on rainy days.

structuredNuance.t: 공기에서 습기를 빼내는 기기. 한국 여름은 장마와 높은 습도 때문에 제습기 수요가 급증하고, 곰팡이 예방과 실내 건조에 쓰이며, 건조기가 없는 집에서는 빨래 말리는 용도로도 자주 씁니다. 동사는 '돌리다/틀다'가 자연스럽습니다.
제습기 = 除濕器, '除(remove)-濕(moisture)-器(device)' — it pulls dampness OUT of the air.
가장 큰 함정은 역시 가습기(加濕器)와의 혼동이에요. 가운데 글자 除(없애다)와 加(더하다)만 다르니, '여름·장마=제습기(뽀송), 겨울=가습기(촉촉)'로 묶어 외우면 안전합니다.
두 번째 함정은 물통 관리예요. 모은 물이 가득 차면 안전을 위해 자동으로 멈추는데, 이를 모르는 초보자는 고장으로 오해하기 쉽습니다 — 사실은 '물통(을) 비우다'를 해 주면 다시 돌아갑니다.

entries.shortExplanation: 가스레인지 means "gas range / gas stove" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
entries.explanation: 가스레인지 (gaseureinji) = "gas range / gas stove". Treat it as a building block that needs a frame: 불 켜다 ("light the burner") shows how it actually behaves. The grammar lives in the particle or ending beside 가스레인지, so notice that piece as you read, not just the dictionary meaning. Begin from a complete sentence about daily routines at home, sleep, doors, windows, and simple requests and swap just one element to make it yours.

usagePhrases.note: 불(을) 켜다 = turn on the flame; 가스불 = the gas flame. For the cooktop itself you can also say 가스레인지 켜다.
가스(를) 잠그다 = close the gas valve (lit. 'lock'); a core safety habit before leaving home.
불(을) 줄이다/키우다 = lower/raise the flame; 불이 세다 = the flame is strong.
The modern alternative; older apartments keep 가스레인지, new builds lean to 인덕션.

examples.ko: 나갈 때 가스 잠갔는지 꼭 확인해.
examples.romanization: nagal ttae gaseu jamganneunji kko kwaginhae.
examples.en: Make sure to check whether you turned off the gas when you leave.
examples.note: Teaches 잠그다 = 'lock/shut a valve'; ~았는지 확인하다 = check whether you did it. A near-universal Korean reminder.

examples.ko: 우리 집은 아직 가스레인지라 냄비 아무거나 다 써요.
examples.romanization: uri jibeun ajik gaseureinjira naembi amugeona da sseoyo.
examples.en: Our place still has a gas range, so I can use any pot at all.
examples.note: Contrasts with induction's pot restriction; teaches 아무거나 다 = 'anything and everything.'

examples.ko: 국 끓을 때까지 가스불 세게 했다가 끓으면 약하게 줄여.
examples.romanization: guk kkeureul ttaekkaji gaseubul sege haetdaga kkeureumyeon yakage juryeo.
examples.en: Keep the gas flame high until the soup boils, then turn it down low.
examples.note: Real cooking register: 세게/약하게 하다 = set high/low; 끓다 = to come to a boil.

entries.nuance: 가스레인지는 'gas + range'를 합친 외래어로, 가스 불꽃으로 직접 조리하는 전통적인 한국식 가열 기구예요(한자어가 아닙니다). 구축 아파트나 오래된 집에 많고, 신축에서는 인덕션으로 대체되는 추세라 두 단어를 비교하는 대화가 흔합니다. 핵심은 안전 표현이에요. 가스 누출·화재 위험 때문에 외출 전 '가스 잠그기'가 생활화돼 있는데, 영어 'turn off the gas'를 그냥 '가스 끄다'로 직역하면 어색합니다 — 밸브를 잠근다는 뜻의 '가스(를) 잠그다'가 정확한 한국어 관용이에요(끄다는 불 자체에). 철자 함정도 흔한데, 표준어는 '가스레인지'지만 일상에서 '가스렌지'로 잘못 쓰는 경우가 매우 많습니다. 인덕션과 달리 냄비 종류를 안 가린다는 점, 불 세기를 '세게/약하게'로 조절한다는 점도 함께 익혀 두세요.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Writing 가스렌지 — the standard spelling is 가스레인지. 가스렌지 is an extremely common but non-standard misspelling.
Saying 가스 끄다 for the leaving-home safety check — Koreans say 가스 잠그다 (close the valve). 끄다 applies to extinguishing the flame, not securing the gas line.
Assuming a gas stove restricts cookware like induction — 가스레인지 heats any pot (냄비 아무거나 다 써요); the magnetic-pot rule is unique to 인덕션.

structuredNuance.t: 가스 불꽃으로 직접 조리하는 전통적인 한국식 가열 기구. 구축 아파트나 오래된 집에 많고, 신축에서는 인덕션으로 대체되는 추세라 두 단어를 비교하는 대화가 흔합니다. 불 세기를 '세게/약하게'로 조절한다는 점도 함께 익혀 두세요.
가스레인지는 'gas + range'를 합친 외래어예요(한자어가 아닙니다).
인덕션과 달리 냄비 종류를 안 가린다는 점도 함께 익혀 두세요. 구축은 가스레인지, 신축은 인덕션으로 기억하면 좋습니다.

핵심은 안전 표현이에요. 가스 누출·화재 위험 때문에 외출 전 '가스 잠그기'가 생활화돼 있는데, 영어 'turn off the gas'를 그냥 '가스 끄다'로 직역하면 어색합니다 — 밸브를 잠근다는 뜻의 '가스(를) 잠그다'가 정확한 한국어 관용이에요(끄다는 불 자체에). 철자 함정도 흔한데, 표준어는 '가스레인지'지만 일상에서 '가스렌지'로 잘못 쓰는 경우가 매우 많습니다.

entries.shortExplanation: 밥솥 means "rice cooker" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
entries.explanation: 밥솥 (bapsot) means "rice cooker". Learn it inside a frame, not as a bare word: a useful first chunk is 밥하다 ("cook rice / make a meal"). In Korean the particle or ending next to 밥솥 signals its job — topic, subject, object, place, time, method, or description — so read the examples for the small piece beside it. Start with one real sentence about daily routines at home, sleep, doors, windows, and simple requests, then change a single part.

usagePhrases.note: 밥(을) 하다 = make rice; 밥솥에 밥하다 is the everyday phrase. 밥 also broadly means 'a meal.'
보온(保溫) = retaining heat; the cooker holds rice warm for hours, a defining feature of a Korean 밥솥.
압력(壓力)밥솥 = the pressure type (e.g. Cuckoo) that makes stickier, glossier rice (찰지다/윤기).
데우다 = warm up; 밥(을) 데우다 reheats cold or refrigerated rice, often in the cooker or microwave.

examples.ko: 밥솥에 밥 해 놨으니까 데워서 먹어.
examples.romanization: bapsote ba pae nwasseunikka dewoseo meogeo.
examples.en: I've made rice in the cooker, so heat it up and eat.
examples.note: Teaches 해 놓다 = 'do in advance'; 데우다 = warm up. A classic Korean family note.

examples.ko: 밥솥 보온으로 오래 두면 밥이 누레져요.
examples.romanization: bapsot booneuro orae dumyeon babi nurejyeoyo.
examples.en: If you leave rice on warm in the cooker too long, it turns yellowish.
examples.note: Teaches 누레지다 (← 누렇다, ㅎ-irregular) = 'turn yellowish'; a real complaint about long keep-warm.

examples.ko: 압력밥솥으로 잡곡밥 하면 훨씬 부드럽고 찰져요.
examples.romanization: amnyeokbapsoteuro japgokba pamyeon hwolssin budeureopgo chaljyeoyo.
examples.en: Multi-grain rice comes out much softer and stickier in a pressure cooker.
examples.note: Real cooking register: 잡곡밥 = mixed-grain rice; 찰지다 = sticky/chewy, the prized texture.

entries.nuance: 밥솥은 순우리말로 '밥(rice)+솥(cauldron)', 즉 밥을 짓는 솥이에요. 오늘날은 거의 다 '전기밥솥'을 가리키며, 한국 가정에서 가장 핵심적인 가전입니다. 어휘 구분 두 가지: 첫째, '솥' 하나만 쓰면 전통적인 무쇠 가마솥을 떠올리니, 일상의 전기 제품은 반드시 '밥솥(전기밥솥)'이라고 해야 해요. 둘째, 쿠쿠·쿠첸 같은 브랜드의 '압력밥솥(壓力밥솥)'은 일반 밥솥보다 밥이 더 찰지고 윤기 나게 지어집니다. 동사는 '요리하다(cook)'를 직역하기보다 '밥(을) 하다'를 쓰는 게 자연스럽고, '보온(保溫)'으로 오래 두면 밥이 누레진다는 표현이 자주 나옵니다. 철자 함정으로, 받침이 ㅌ인 '밥솥'을 발음대로 '밥속'으로 잘못 쓰는 경우가 많으니 주의하세요(밥솥 → [밥쏟]).
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Saying just 솥 for the appliance — 솥 alone suggests a traditional cast-iron cauldron. For the everyday electric machine, say 밥솥 (or 전기밥솥).
Mis-spelling it 밥속 — the final consonant is ㅌ, so it's 밥솥 (pronounced [밥쏟]). 밥속 means 'inside the rice,' a different thing.
Using 요리하다 for cooking rice — the natural verb is 밥(을) 하다 / 밥(을) 짓다, not a literal translation of English 'cook.'

structuredNuance.t: 밥을 짓는 솥. 오늘날은 거의 다 '전기밥솥'을 가리키며, 한국 가정에서 가장 핵심적인 가전입니다. 동사는 '요리하다(cook)'를 직역하기보다 '밥(을) 하다'를 쓰는 게 자연스럽고, '보온(保溫)'으로 오래 두면 밥이 누레진다는 표현이 자주 나옵니다.
밥솥은 순우리말로 '밥(rice)+솥(cauldron)', 즉 밥을 짓는 솥이에요.
'솥' 하나만 쓰면 전통적인 무쇠 가마솥을 떠올리니, 일상의 전기 제품은 반드시 '밥솥(전기밥솥)'이라고 해야 해요. 또 쿠쿠·쿠첸 같은 브랜드의 '압력밥솥(壓力밥솥)'은 일반 밥솥보다 밥이 더 찰지고 윤기 나게 지어집니다.
철자 함정으로, 받침이 ㅌ인 '밥솥'을 발음대로 '밥속'으로 잘못 쓰는 경우가 많으니 주의하세요(밥솥 → [밥쏟]).

entries.shortExplanation: 멀티탭 means "power strip / multi-outlet" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
entries.explanation: "power strip / multi-outlet" is 멀티탭 (meoltitaep). The word itself is easy; what matters is the company it keeps, like 콘센트 ("wall outlet"). Watch the particle attached to 멀티탭 in each example — that little marker, not the word, tells you whether it is the topic, the subject, the object, or a place. Copy one full sentence about daily routines at home, sleep, doors, windows, and simple requests first, then vary one word.

usagePhrases.note: 콘센트 = the wall socket (itself a loanword, from 'concentric plug'); a 멀티탭 plugs into a 콘센트.
플러그를 콘센트/멀티탭에 꽂다 = plug in. 꽂다 = insert/stick in; opposite is 빼다 (unplug).
문어발(식) = plugging too many devices into one strip; warned against as a 화재 위험 (fire hazard).
대기전력(待機電力) = standby power; per-socket switches let you cut it to save on the electric bill.

examples.ko: 콘센트가 부족해서 멀티탭 하나 더 샀어요.
examples.romanization: konsenteuga bujokaeseo meoltitae pana deo sasseoyo.
examples.en: There weren't enough outlets, so I bought another power strip.
examples.note: Teaches 부족하다 = 'be insufficient'; 하나 더 = one more. A classic studio-apartment problem.

examples.ko: 충전기 멀티탭에 꽂아 놨어. 저기 스위치 켜면 돼.
examples.romanization: chungjeongi meoltitaebe kkoja nwasseo. jeogi seuwichi kyeomyeon dwae.
examples.en: I plugged the charger into the power strip. Just flip that switch.
examples.note: Teaches 꽂아 놓다 = 'have it plugged in'; many strips have a per-socket 스위치.

examples.ko: 멀티탭에 문어발로 다 꽂으면 과부하 걸려서 위험해요.
examples.romanization: meoltitaebe muneoballo da kkojeumyeon gwabuha geollyeoseo wiheomhaeyo.
examples.en: Plugging everything into one strip octopus-style overloads it and is dangerous.
examples.note: Real safety register: 문어발 = overloading; 과부하(가) 걸리다 = it gets overloaded.

entries.nuance: 멀티탭은 영어 'multi-tap'에서 온 콩글리시로, 콘센트 하나에 꽂아 여러 기기를 연결하는 멀티 콘센트(개별 스위치가 달린 것이 많음)를 가리켜요. 한국 원룸·자취방은 벽 콘센트가 부족한 경우가 많아 거의 필수품이고, 개별 스위치로 대기전력을 차단해 전기세를 아끼기도 합니다. 가장 큰 함정은 두 가지예요. 첫째, '멀티탭(여러 구짜리 연결 기구)'과 '콘센트(벽에 박힌 소켓)'는 서로 다른 물건인데, 영어 화자는 멀티탭까지 뭉뚱그려 outlet/socket이라 부르며 콘센트라고 잘못 말하기 쉽습니다. 둘째, 영어 'power strip'을 직역하거나 영어 단어를 그대로 쓰면 한국에서는 못 알아들으니, 반드시 '멀티탭'이라고 해야 통해요. 안전 표현으로 '문어발(식 콘센트)'은 과부하·화재 경고에 단골로 등장하니 함께 익혀 두세요.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Calling the strip a 콘센트 — 콘센트 is the fixed wall socket; the multi-outlet strip you plug into it is a 멀티탭. They are different objects.
Using English 'power strip' and expecting to be understood — in Korea you must say 멀티탭 (Konglish from 'multi-tap'); the English term won't register.
Ignoring the 문어발 warning — overloading one strip (문어발식) causes 과부하 (overload) and is a recognized fire hazard, not just a tidiness issue.

structuredNuance.t: 콘센트 하나에 꽂아 여러 기기를 연결하는 멀티 콘센트(개별 스위치가 달린 것이 많음). 한국 원룸·자취방은 벽 콘센트가 부족한 경우가 많아 거의 필수품이고, 개별 스위치로 대기전력을 차단해 전기세를 아끼기도 합니다. 안전 표현으로 '문어발(식 콘센트)'은 과부하·화재 경고에 단골로 등장하니 함께 익혀 두세요.
멀티탭은 영어 'multi-tap'에서 온 콩글리시예요.
'멀티탭(여러 구짜리 연결 기구)'과 '콘센트(벽에 박힌 소켓)'는 서로 다른 물건인데, 영어 화자는 멀티탭까지 뭉뚱그려 outlet/socket이라 부르며 콘센트라고 잘못 말하기 쉽습니다.
영어 'power strip'을 직역하거나 영어 단어를 그대로 쓰면 한국에서는 못 알아들으니, 반드시 '멀티탭'이라고 해야 통해요.

entries.shortExplanation: 리모컨 means "remote control" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
entries.explanation: 리모컨 (rimokeon) = "remote control". Treat it as a building block that needs a frame: 건전지 ("dry-cell battery") shows how it actually behaves. The grammar lives in the particle or ending beside 리모컨, so notice that piece as you read, not just the dictionary meaning. Begin from a complete sentence about daily routines at home, sleep, doors, windows, and simple requests and swap just one element to make it yours.

usagePhrases.note: 건전지(乾電池)(를) 갈다 = change the AA/AAA cells a 리모컨 runs on. 갈다 = swap a consumable.
채널(을) 돌리다 = flip channels; 돌리다 ('turn') lingers from the old dial-TV era.
볼륨(을) 키우다/줄이다 = raise/lower the volume via the remote. 키우다 = increase, 줄이다 = decrease.
리모컨 attaches to many devices, so you specify: 에어컨 리모컨, TV 리모컨, 셋톱박스 리모컨.

examples.ko: 리모컨 어디 갔어? 소파 밑에 있나 봐.
examples.romanization: rimokeon eodi gasseo? sopa mite inna bwa.
examples.en: Where did the remote go? It might be under the couch.
examples.note: Teaches 어디 갔어? = 'where did it go?'; ~나 봐 = 'looks like / I guess.' The universal lost-remote line.

examples.ko: 리모컨 건전지 다 됐나 봐. 채널이 안 돌아가.
examples.romanization: rimokeon geonjeonji da dwaenna bwa. chaeneori an doraga.
examples.en: Looks like the remote's batteries died. The channels won't change.
examples.note: Teaches 건전지 다 되다 = 'batteries are dead'; 안 돌아가다 = won't respond/change.

examples.ko: 에어컨 리모컨으로 온도 좀 낮추고 바람 약하게 해 줄래?
examples.romanization: eeokeol limokeoneuro ondo jom natchugo baram yakage hae jullae?
examples.en: Can you lower the temperature and set the airflow to low with the AC remote?
examples.note: Real-situation register: 온도(를) 낮추다 = lower the temp; 바람(을) 약하게 하다 = weaken the airflow; 줄래? soft request.

entries.nuance: 리모컨은 영어 'remote control'을 줄여 들여온 콩글리시로, TV·에어컨·셋톱박스 등 거의 모든 가전에 딸려 와 집집마다 여러 개가 굴러다녀요 — 그래서 '리모컨 어디 갔어?'는 한국 가정의 단골 대사죠. 함정 세 가지: 첫째, 표준 표기는 '리모컨'인데 '리모콘'으로 잘못 쓰는 경우가 매우 흔합니다. 둘째, 전원은 충전이 아니라 'AA/AAA 건전지(乾電池)'로 돌아가므로, 영어 'charge the remote' 감각으로 '리모컨 충전하다'라고 하면 어색하고 '건전지 갈다(교체하다)'가 맞아요. 셋째, 기기마다 리모컨이 따로라 그냥 '리모컨'만 하면 어떤 건지 모호하니 'TV 리모컨', '에어컨 리모컨'처럼 앞에 기기를 붙입니다. 채널은 '돌리다', 볼륨·온도는 '키우다/줄이다·낮추다'로 조절한다는 동사 짝도 함께 익혀 두세요.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Spelling it 리모콘 — the standard form is 리모컨. 리모콘 is a very frequent misspelling.
Saying 리모컨 충전하다 — a normal remote runs on replaceable 건전지 (dry cells), not a rechargeable battery. The correct phrase is 건전지 갈다 (change the batteries).
Saying bare 리모컨 when several exist — specify the device (TV 리모컨, 에어컨 리모컨); otherwise it's unclear which remote you mean.

structuredNuance.t: TV·에어컨·셋톱박스 등 거의 모든 가전에 딸려 오는 원격 조종기로, 집집마다 여러 개가 굴러다녀요 — 그래서 '리모컨 어디 갔어?'는 한국 가정의 단골 대사죠. 채널은 '돌리다', 볼륨·온도는 '키우다/줄이다·낮추다'로 조절한다는 동사 짝도 함께 익혀 두세요.
리모컨은 영어 'remote control'을 줄여 들여온 콩글리시예요.

표준 표기는 '리모컨'인데 '리모콘'으로 잘못 쓰는 경우가 매우 흔합니다. 또 전원은 충전이 아니라 'AA/AAA 건전지(乾電池)'로 돌아가므로, 영어 'charge the remote' 감각으로 '리모컨 충전하다'라고 하면 어색하고 '건전지 갈다(교체하다)'가 맞아요. 끝으로 기기마다 리모컨이 따로라 그냥 '리모컨'만 하면 어떤 건지 모호하니 'TV 리모컨', '에어컨 리모컨'처럼 앞에 기기를 붙입니다.

entries.shortExplanation: 손목 means "wrist" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
entries.explanation: 손목 (sonmok) means "wrist". Learn it inside a frame, not as a bare word: a useful first chunk is 손목이 아파요 ("My wrist hurts"). In Korean the particle or ending next to 손목 signals its job — topic, subject, object, place, time, method, or description — so read the examples for the small piece beside it. Start with one real sentence about saying what hurts, asking for rest, and explaining basic health needs, then change a single part.

usagePhrases.note: Subject particle 이 marks the body part that hurts — the default clinic line
삐다 takes 을/를: you sprain a specific joint
Romance-drama staple; note 을, you grab the wrist itself
One word: 손목 + 시계 (時計, 'time-meter') — the watch, not the body part

examples.en: My wrist hurts a little.
examples.note: Simplest clinic sentence — body part + 이 + 아파요

examples.ko: 마우스를 오래 써서 손목이 너무 시큰거려요.
examples.romanization: mauseureul orae sseoseo sonmogi neomu sikeungeoryeoyo.
examples.en: My wrist really aches from using the mouse too long.
examples.note: 시큰거리다 = a dull, repetitive joint ache, the desk-job complaint

examples.ko: 넘어질 때 손으로 바닥을 짚다가 손목을 삐었어요.
examples.romanization: neomeojil ttae soneuro badageul jipdaga sonmogeul ppieosseoyo.
examples.en: I sprained my wrist when I braced my fall with my hand.
examples.note: real injury story: 짚다(brace) → 삐다(sprain), past 삐었어요

entries.nuance: 손목 is the wrist joint, built transparently from 손(hand) + 목(neck) — Korean treats it as the 'neck of the hand,' the same logic behind 발목(ankle). The key contrast is with bare 손: 손 is the whole hand, so if you specifically twisted or strained the joint you must say 손목, not 손, or a Korean pictures the palm/fingers instead. Register is plain and neutral — fine for friends and equally fine at the 정형외과(orthopedic clinic), where 손목이 아파요 and 손목을 삐었어요 are everyday lines. Habitual collocations: 손목이 시큰거리다(aches), 손목에 무리가 가다(gets strained), 손목을 삐다/접질리다(sprain). The English-speaker pitfall is the particle on 삐다: English says 'sprain my wrist,' so learners reach for 손목에, but 삐다 takes the object marker — 손목을 삐었어요.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Saying 손 아파요 when you actually hurt the joint — 손 is the whole hand; to be precise about the joint say 손목이 아파요.
Using 에 with 삐다 by analogy to English ('sprain in my wrist'): it is 손목을 삐었어요 with the object marker 을, not 손목에 삐었어요.
Calling the watch 손목 — the body part is 손목, the watch is 손목시계.

structuredNuance.t: 손목 is the wrist joint. Register is plain and neutral — fine for friends and equally fine at the 정형외과(orthopedic clinic), where 손목이 아파요 and 손목을 삐었어요 are everyday lines. Habitual collocations: 손목이 시큰거리다(aches), 손목에 무리가 가다(gets strained), 손목을 삐다/접질리다(sprain).

entries.shortExplanation: 발목 means "ankle" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
entries.explanation: "ankle" is 발목 (balmok). The word itself is easy; what matters is the company it keeps, like 발목을 삐다 ("to sprain one's ankle"). Watch the particle attached to 발목 in each example — that little marker, not the word, tells you whether it is the topic, the subject, the object, or a place. Copy one full sentence about saying what hurts, asking for rest, and explaining basic health needs first, then vary one word.

usagePhrases.note: The #1 ankle complaint; object marker 을 on the joint
붓다 is ㅅ-irregular → 부어요 / 부었어요
접질리다 = a sharper 'rolled it' nuance than 삐다
Idiom: literally 'grab the ankle' = drag down / be a burden

examples.en: My ankle is a bit swollen.
examples.note: Note the ㅅ-irregular: 붓다 → 부었어요, never 붓었어요

examples.en: I sprained my ankle on the stairs and walked with a limp.
examples.note: 절뚝거리다 = to limp — a vivid everyday result of a sprain

examples.ko: 내가 실수해서 괜히 팀 발목을 잡은 것 같아요.
examples.romanization: naega silsuhaeseo gwaenhi tim balmogeul jabeun geot gatayo.
examples.en: I feel like my mistake dragged the whole team down.
examples.note: 발목을 잡다 used figuratively — to hold/hinder, not literal

entries.nuance: 발목 is the ankle, formed as 발(foot) + 목(neck) — the 'neck of the foot,' parallel to 손목. Distinguish it from bare 발(the whole foot): if you rolled the joint, 발목을 삐었어요 is precise, whereas 발 아파요 just means your foot hurts somewhere. It is plain, neutral register and the staple phrase at the 정형외과(整形外科, orthopedics): 발목을 삐다/접질리다, 발목이 붓다/시큰거리다. 발목까지 오는 바지 (ankle-length pants) shows the same word in clothes-shopping. Two English-speaker pitfalls: first, 붓다 is ㅅ-irregular, so it conjugates 부어요/부었어요 (drop the ㅅ), and learners wrongly write 붓어요. Second, the idiom 발목을 잡다 means to hold someone back or be a burden — don't read it literally.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Saying 발 아파요 when you specifically twisted the ankle joint — use 발목 to be precise: 발목을 삐었어요.
Conjugating 붓다 as 붓어요 — it is ㅅ-irregular, so the ㅅ drops: 부어요 / 부었어요.
Reading 발목을 잡다 literally as physically grabbing — in most contexts it is the idiom 'to hold back / be a drag.'

structuredNuance.t: 발목 is the ankle. It is plain, neutral register and the staple phrase at the 정형외과(整形外科, orthopedics): 발목을 삐다/접질리다, 발목이 붓다/시큰거리다. 발목까지 오는 바지 (ankle-length pants) shows the same word in clothes-shopping.
Distinguish it from bare 발(the whole foot): if you rolled the joint, 발목을 삐었어요 is precise, whereas 발 아파요 just means your foot hurts somewhere.

entries.shortExplanation: 팔꿈치 means "elbow" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
entries.explanation: 팔꿈치 (palkkumchi) = "elbow". Treat it as a building block that needs a frame: 팔꿈치가 아파요 ("My elbow hurts") shows how it actually behaves. The grammar lives in the particle or ending beside 팔꿈치, so notice that piece as you read, not just the dictionary meaning. Begin from a complete sentence about saying what hurts, asking for rest, and explaining basic health needs and swap just one element to make it yours.

usagePhrases.note: Standard clinic phrase; 이 marks the aching joint

usagePhrases.en: to prop oneself on one's elbow
usagePhrases.note: 괴다 = to prop up; classic bored-meeting posture
Instrument particle 로: '(by means of) the elbow'
까지다 = skin gets scraped off, intransitive

examples.en: My elbow hurts a bit.
examples.note: Simplest form — joint + 이 + 아파요

examples.en: I dozed off propped up on my elbow on the desk.
examples.note: 팔꿈치를 괴다 = the prop-your-chin posture; 에 marks where (책상에)

examples.ko: 테니스를 친 뒤로 팔꿈치 바깥쪽이 계속 아파요.
examples.romanization: teniseureul chin dwiro palkkumchi bakkatjjogi gyesok apayo.
examples.en: The outside of my elbow has hurt ever since I played tennis.
examples.note: real 'tennis elbow' description with location 바깥쪽(outer side)

entries.nuance: 팔꿈치 is the elbow joint, written as one word from 팔(arm) + 꿈치 with the tense consonant ㄲ. There is no everyday near-synonym — the medical term 주관절(肘關節, elbow joint) exists but nobody uses it in conversation, so 팔꿈치 covers all registers. Habitual collocations: 팔꿈치를 괴다(prop on), 팔꿈치로 찌르다(nudge with — note instrument 로), 팔꿈치가 까지다(scrape), 팔꿈치가 아프다(ache, e.g. tennis elbow). The biggest English-speaker pitfall here is spelling/pronunciation: learners write 팔꿉치 or 팔굼치, but only 팔꿈치 is correct, and you must keep the 팔 — bare 꿈치 is not a word. A second trap is the particle on 찌르다: you nudge 'with' the elbow, so it's 팔꿈치로, not 팔꿈치를.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Misspelling it as 팔꿉치 or 팔굼치 — the only correct form is 팔꿈치 (note ㄲ and ㅁ받침).
Dropping 팔 and saying just 꿈치 — the full word is always 팔꿈치.
Using 을/를 with 찌르다 for the nudging hand — it's the instrument particle: 팔꿈치로 찔렀어요.

structuredNuance.t: 팔꿈치 is the elbow joint, covering all registers in everyday speech. Habitual collocations: 팔꿈치를 괴다(prop on), 팔꿈치로 찌르다(nudge with — note instrument 로), 팔꿈치가 까지다(scrape), 팔꿈치가 아프다(ache, e.g. tennis elbow).
There is no everyday near-synonym — the medical term 주관절(肘關節, elbow joint) exists but nobody uses it in conversation, so 팔꿈치 covers all registers.

entries.shortExplanation: 발가락 means "toe" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
entries.explanation: 발가락 (balgarak) means "toe". Learn it inside a frame, not as a bare word: a useful first chunk is 발가락을 찧다 ("to stub one's toe"). In Korean the particle or ending next to 발가락 signals its job — topic, subject, object, place, time, method, or description — so read the examples for the small piece beside it. Start with one real sentence about saying what hurts, asking for rest, and explaining basic health needs, then change a single part.

usagePhrases.note: 찧다 = to bang hard against something; object marker 을
엄지(the 'thumb/biggest one') + 발가락, one word
새끼 = the smallest/baby one; the toe you stub at night
사이 = the gap; where 무좀(athlete's foot) starts

examples.en: My toe hurts.
examples.note: Plain base sentence

examples.en: The shoes are small so my toes feel cramped.
examples.note: 꽉 끼다 = packed/cramped tight — shoe-fitting vocab

examples.ko: 밤에 문턱에 새끼발가락을 찧어서 눈물이 났어요.
examples.romanization: bame munteoge saekkibalgarageul jjieoseo nunmuri nasseoyo.
examples.en: I stubbed my pinky toe on the door frame at night and my eyes watered.
examples.note: real-situation: the universal night-time injury, 찧다 in past tense

entries.nuance: 발가락 is a toe, built from 발(foot) + 가락(digit/strand), exactly parallel to 손가락(finger) — once you see the 가락 pattern both words click. Name individual toes with 엄지발가락(big toe, lit. 'thumb-toe') and 새끼발가락(pinky toe, lit. 'baby-toe'). Don't confuse 발가락(toe) with 발톱(toenail): 톱 is the nail, so 'I cut my toenails' is 발톱을 깎다, not 발가락. Register is fully neutral and casual-safe. Typical collocations: 발가락을 찧다(stub), 발가락이 꽉 끼다(toes feel cramped in shoes), 발가락 사이가 가렵다(itchy between the toes). The English-speaker pitfall is the verb for stubbing — English 'stub' has no direct cognate; Korean uses 찧다 (bang hard) with the object marker: 발가락을 찧었어요.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Confusing 발가락(toe) with 발톱(toenail) — the nail is 발톱, so trimming nails is 발톱을 깎다.
Misspelling it 발까락 — it is 발가락 with plain ㄱ, even though it sounds tensed.
Reaching for a word like 차다/때리다 to say 'stub' — the natural verb is 찧다: 발가락을 찧었어요.

entries.shortExplanation: 허벅지 means "thigh" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
entries.explanation: "thigh" is 허벅지 (heobeokji). The word itself is easy; what matters is the company it keeps, like 허벅지가 굵다 ("to have thick thighs"). Watch the particle attached to 허벅지 in each example — that little marker, not the word, tells you whether it is the topic, the subject, the object, or a place. Copy one full sentence about saying what hurts, asking for rest, and explaining basic health needs first, then vary one word.

usagePhrases.note: 굵다 (thick in girth) for limbs — not 두껍다
근육 (筋肉, 'muscle'); gym vocabulary
안쪽 = inner side; back of thigh is 허벅지 뒤

usagePhrases.en: for the thighs to feel tight
usagePhrases.note: 당기다 = a pulled/stretched-tight sensation after exercise

examples.en: My thighs are sore.
examples.note: Base sentence after any leg workout

examples.en: The jeans are tight around the thighs.
examples.note: 꽉 끼다 + location 에서 — a real fitting problem for muscular legs

examples.ko: 스쿼트를 했더니 허벅지 안쪽이 너무 당겨요.
examples.romanization: seukwoteureul haetdeoni heobeokji anjjogi neomu danggyeoyo.
examples.en: After doing squats, my inner thighs feel really tight.
examples.note: 당기다 = the post-workout pulled-tight feeling, with 안쪽(inner)

entries.nuance: 허벅지 is the thigh — the thick upper leg above the knee. The contrast to learn is register, not body part: 허벅지 is the normal spoken word, while 대퇴부(大腿部, 'big-leg region') is the clinical/anatomical term you'll only meet in a hospital or textbook — say 허벅지 in real life. Specify regions with 허벅지 안쪽(inner) and 허벅지 뒤(back/hamstring). A vocabulary pitfall for English speakers: 'thick thighs' uses 굵다 (thick in circumference, for cylindrical things like legs and arms), NOT 두껍다 (thick in flat thickness, for books/blankets) — 허벅지가 굵다 is right, 허벅지가 두껍다 sounds off. Other collocations: 허벅지가 당기다(feel tight/pulled), 허벅지가 저리다(go numb), 허벅지 근육(thigh muscle). Also keep it distinct from 종아리(calf), which is the lower leg.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Using 두껍다 for thick thighs — limbs take 굵다 (girth): 허벅지가 굵다, not 허벅지가 두껍다.
Reaching for 대퇴부 in casual talk — that is the clinical term; ordinary speech is 허벅지.
Confusing 허벅지(thigh, upper leg) with 종아리(calf, lower leg).

structuredNuance.t: 허벅지 is the thigh — the thick upper leg above the knee. Specify regions with 허벅지 안쪽(inner) and 허벅지 뒤(back/hamstring). Other collocations: 허벅지가 당기다(feel tight/pulled), 허벅지가 저리다(go numb), 허벅지 근육(thigh muscle).

The contrast to learn is register, not body part: 허벅지 is the normal spoken word, while 대퇴부(大腿部, 'big-leg region') is the clinical/anatomical term you'll only meet in a hospital or textbook — say 허벅지 in real life. Also keep it distinct from 종아리(calf), which is the lower leg.

entries.shortExplanation: 종아리 means "calf (lower leg)" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
entries.explanation: 종아리 (jongari) = "calf (lower leg)". Treat it as a building block that needs a frame: 종아리가 뭉치다 ("for the calf to knot up") shows how it actually behaves. The grammar lives in the particle or ending beside 종아리, so notice that piece as you read, not just the dictionary meaning. Begin from a complete sentence about saying what hurts, asking for rest, and explaining basic health needs and swap just one element to make it yours.

usagePhrases.en: for the calf to knot up
usagePhrases.note: 뭉치다 = muscle stiffens into a knot
쥐가 나다 = idiom for a cramp; note 에 marks the spot
굵다 for limb girth, not 두껍다
알 = the rounded muscle belly of the calf

examples.en: My calf hurts.
examples.note: Plain base sentence

examples.en: My calves got really tight from wearing heels.
examples.note: 뭉치다 = knotted/stiff; classic end-of-day complaint

examples.en: I woke up because I got a cramp in my calf.
examples.note: 쥐가 나다 in a real situation; 에 marks where the cramp struck

entries.nuance: 종아리 is the calf — the fleshy muscle on the BACK of the lower leg, the opposite face from 정강이(the bony shin in front); mixing those two is the most common confusion, so anchor it as 'calf = soft back, shin = hard front.' Register is plain and neutral. Its signature collocation is the idiom 쥐가 나다 — literally 'a mouse comes out,' meaning to get a sudden cramp; never translate 쥐(mouse) literally, and note it pairs with the location particle 에 (종아리에 쥐가 났어요). Other habitual phrases: 종아리가 뭉치다(knot up), 종아리가 퉁퉁 붓다(swell up), 종아리 알(the muscle bulge), 종아리 마사지(calf massage). Like other limbs, 'thick calves' is 종아리가 굵다 with 굵다(girth), not 두껍다.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Swapping 종아리(calf, soft back of lower leg) and 정강이(shin, hard front) — remember calf = back, shin = front.
Translating 쥐가 나다 literally — 쥐 means 'mouse' but the phrase just means 'to cramp': 종아리에 쥐가 났어요.
Using 두껍다 for thick calves — limbs use 굵다: 종아리가 굵다.

entries.shortExplanation: 정강이 means "shin" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
entries.explanation: 정강이 (jeonggangi) means "shin". Learn it inside a frame, not as a bare word: a useful first chunk is 정강이를 부딪히다 ("to bang one's shin"). In Korean the particle or ending next to 정강이 signals its job — topic, subject, object, place, time, method, or description — so read the examples for the small piece beside it. Start with one real sentence about saying what hurts, asking for rest, and explaining basic health needs, then change a single part.

usagePhrases.note: 부딪히다 = to collide/knock against something

usagePhrases.en: to get kicked in the shin
usagePhrases.note: 차이다 = passive of 차다, '(I) get kicked'
뼈 = bone; the hard ridge you feel up front
까지다 = skin gets scraped off

examples.en: My shin hurts.
examples.note: Base sentence

examples.ko: 침대 모서리에 정강이를 부딪혀서 멍이 들었어요.
examples.romanization: chimdae moseorie jeonggangireul budityeoseo meongi deureosseoyo.
examples.en: I banged my shin on the corner of the bed and got a bruise.
examples.note: 멍이 들다 = to bruise; 에 marks what you hit (모서리에)

examples.en: I got kicked in the shin by the opposing player during soccer.
examples.note: passive 차이다 with agent 한테 — you receive the kick, not give it

entries.nuance: 정강이 is the shin — the hard, bony front ridge of the lower leg, the exact opposite of 종아리(the soft calf at the back); fix them as 'shin = hard front, calf = soft back.' Because it is bone with almost no padding (살이 없다), knocking it on furniture is a uniquely sharp pain everyone relates to, which is why 부딪히다 collocations are so common. The bone itself is 정강이뼈. Register is plain and neutral. The standout English-speaker pitfall is voice: when something hits YOU, Korean uses the passive — 차이다('get kicked') and 부딪히다('get bumped/knock into'), so 'I got kicked in the shin' is 정강이를 차였어요, and the kicker is marked with 한테/에게. Beginners wrongly use the active 차다('I kick'), which reverses who did it. Note the particle: even in the passive, the shin is marked 을/를 (정강이를 차이다).
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Confusing 정강이(shin, hard front) with 종아리(calf, soft back) — anchor: shin = front, calf = back.
Using active 차다/부딪다 when you were the one hit — use the passive 차이다/부딪히다: 정강이를 차였어요.
Marking the kicker with 이/가 — the agent of the passive takes 한테/에게: 상대 선수한테 차였어요.

entries.shortExplanation: 뒤통수 means "back of the head" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
entries.explanation: "back of the head" is 뒤통수 (dwitongsu). The word itself is easy; what matters is the company it keeps, like 뒤통수를 맞다 ("to get hit on the back of the head / to be betrayed"). Watch the particle attached to 뒤통수 in each example — that little marker, not the word, tells you whether it is the topic, the subject, the object, or a place. Copy one full sentence about saying what hurts, asking for rest, and explaining basic health needs first, then vary one word.

usagePhrases.en: to get hit on the back of the head / to be betrayed
usagePhrases.note: Literal or figurative — context decides
Very common idiom; literally 'strike the back of the head'
납작하다 = flat; a real Korean appearance remark

usagePhrases.en: to feel stares on the back of one's head
usagePhrases.note: 따갑다 = to sting/prickle; idiom for being watched

examples.en: The back of my head hurts.
examples.note: Plain literal base sentence

examples.ko: 선반 모서리에 뒤통수를 부딪혀서 혹이 났어요.
examples.romanization: seonban moseorie dwitongsureul budityeoseo hogi nasseoyo.
examples.en: I hit the back of my head on the shelf corner and got a bump.
examples.note: literal physical use; 혹이 나다 = to get a lump

examples.en: I got stabbed in the back by a friend I trusted.
examples.note: figurative betrayal — the most common real use; agent takes 한테

entries.nuance: 뒤통수 is the back of the head, from 뒤(back) + 통수, and it lives a double life. Literally it is where you bump your head (뒤통수를 부딪히다, 혹이 나다). Figuratively, 뒤통수를 치다 / 뒤통수를 맞다 is an extremely common idiom for betraying or being betrayed behind one's back — so in any social context 뒤통수를 맞았어요 almost always means 'I got backstabbed,' not a literal blow. Register is casual; in formal or medical speech you'd switch to 뒷머리 or the Sino-Korean 후두부(後頭部, 'back-head region'). Note also that Koreans genuinely judge head shape — saying someone's 뒤통수가 납작하다(flat) vs round is normal small talk. The pitfall for English speakers is exactly that idiom: don't take 뒤통수를 맞다 literally when the topic is trust, and mark the betrayer with 한테/에게.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Taking 뒤통수를 맞았어요 literally in a social context — it almost always means 'I was betrayed.'
Using 뒤통수 in formal or medical speech — there you'd say 뒷머리 or 후두부; 뒤통수 is casual.
Marking the betrayer with 이/가 in the idiom — use 한테/에게: 친구한테 뒤통수를 맞았어요.

entries.shortExplanation: 손바닥 means "palm (of the hand)" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
entries.explanation: 손바닥 (sonbadak) = "palm (of the hand)". Treat it as a building block that needs a frame: 손바닥을 펴다 ("to open one's palm") shows how it actually behaves. The grammar lives in the particle or ending beside 손바닥, so notice that piece as you read, not just the dictionary meaning. Begin from a complete sentence about saying what hurts, asking for rest, and explaining basic health needs and swap just one element to make it yours.

usagePhrases.note: 펴다 = to spread/unfold open
에 marks the spot; 땀이 나다 = sweat comes out
만 하다 = 'only as big as' → idiom for very small

usagePhrases.en: to hide the sky with a palm
usagePhrases.note: Proverb: to try to cover up the obvious

examples.en: My palm is itchy.
examples.note: Base sentence; 손바닥이 + adjective

examples.en: I braced my fall with my palms.
examples.note: instrument 으로 = used the palm to brace; 짚다 = to prop

examples.ko: 우리 집은 손바닥만 해서 짐 둘 데가 없어요.
examples.romanization: uri jibeun sonbadangman haeseo jim dul dega eopseoyo.
examples.en: Our place is so tiny there's nowhere to put things.
examples.note: 손바닥만 하다 used figuratively for 'tiny' — a cramped apartment

entries.nuance: 손바닥 is the palm — the inner flat surface of the hand, from 손(hand) + 바닥(floor/flat bottom). Its built-in opposite is 손등(back of the hand), where 등 means 'back'; keep the pair 바닥(inner)↔등(outer) straight, since beginners mix them. Register is neutral. The standout idiom is 손바닥만 하다, literally 'only the size of a palm,' used to call something very small — most often a cramped apartment (집이 손바닥만 하다); treat it as figurative, not a real measurement. There's also a well-known proverb 손바닥으로 하늘을 가리다 ('cover the sky with your palm' = futilely hide what everyone can see). Typical collocations: 손바닥을 펴다(open the palm), 손바닥에 땀이 나다(sweaty palms from nerves), 손바닥으로 바닥을 짚다(brace with palms). The pitfall is the instrument particle: you brace 'with' the palm → 손바닥으로, not 손바닥을.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Confusing 손바닥(palm, inner) with 손등(back of the hand) — 바닥 is the inner flat side, 등 is the outer back.
Taking 손바닥만 하다 as a literal measurement — it is the idiom 'tiny / palm-sized.'
Using 손바닥을 짚다 to mean 'brace with your palm' — the instrument particle is 으로: 손바닥으로 짚었어요.

entries.shortExplanation: 발바닥 means "sole (of the foot)" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
entries.explanation: 발바닥 (balbadak) means "sole (of the foot)". Learn it inside a frame, not as a bare word: a useful first chunk is 발바닥이 아파요 ("My soles hurt"). In Korean the particle or ending next to 발바닥 signals its job — topic, subject, object, place, time, method, or description — so read the examples for the small piece beside it. Start with one real sentence about saying what hurts, asking for rest, and explaining basic health needs, then change a single part.

usagePhrases.note: After a long day of walking; 이 marks the sole

usagePhrases.en: to get a blister on the sole
usagePhrases.note: 물집이 잡히다 = a blister forms (set phrase)
Idiom: feel like they're on fire from walking
지압 (指壓, 'finger-press') = acupressure

examples.en: The soles of my feet are itchy.
examples.note: Base sentence; 발바닥이 + adjective

examples.ko: 새 구두를 신고 발바닥에 물집이 잡혔어요.
examples.romanization: sae gudureul singo balbadage muljibi japyeosseoyo.
examples.en: I got blisters on my soles from new dress shoes.
examples.note: 물집이 잡히다 = blister forms — never 물집을 만들다

examples.ko: 하루 종일 걸었더니 발바닥에 불이 나는 것 같아요.
examples.romanization: haru jongil georeotdeoni balbadage buri naneun geot gatayo.
examples.en: After walking all day, my soles feel like they're on fire.
examples.note: 불이 나다 used figuratively for burning fatigue

entries.nuance: 발바닥 is the sole — the flat underside of the foot, from 발(foot) + 바닥(floor/flat bottom), mirroring 손바닥(palm). Its opposite is 발등(the top of the foot, where 등 = 'back/upper side'); don't confuse the underside 바닥 with the top 등. Register is neutral, and it shows up constantly after long walks, with blisters, and at the 지압(指壓, acupressure) and foot-massage shops that are popular in Korea. The crucial collocation pitfall for English speakers is blisters: a blister 'forms' or 'is caught' — 물집이 잡히다 / 물집이 생기다, with the blister as the SUBJECT (이/가) — so it's 발바닥에 물집이 잡혔어요, never the English-style 물집을 만들다('make a blister'). Other set phrases: 발바닥에 불이 나다(soles burning, figurative) and 발바닥이 화끈거리다(soles feel hot).
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Confusing 발바닥(sole, underside) with 발등(top of the foot) — 바닥 is the bottom, 등 is the upper side.
Saying 물집을 만들다 for getting a blister — the blister forms on its own: 물집이 잡히다 / 물집이 생기다.
Using 손바닥 (palm) when you mean the foot — for the foot it is 발바닥.

entries.shortExplanation: 겨드랑이 means "armpit" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
entries.explanation: "armpit" is 겨드랑이 (gyeodeurangi). The word itself is easy; what matters is the company it keeps, like 겨드랑이에 땀이 나다 ("to sweat under the arms"). Watch the particle attached to 겨드랑이 in each example — that little marker, not the word, tells you whether it is the topic, the subject, the object, or a place. Copy one full sentence about saying what hurts, asking for rest, and explaining basic health needs first, then vary one word.

usagePhrases.note: 에 marks the spot; 땀이 나다 = sweat comes out
냄새 = smell; 암내 is the blunter word for body odor
제모 (除毛, 'remove-hair') = hair removal

usagePhrases.en: to feel a lump in the armpit
usagePhrases.note: 멍울 = lump (e.g. lymph node); 잡히다 = is felt

examples.en: My armpit is itchy.
examples.note: Base sentence; 겨드랑이 + 가 + adjective

examples.ko: 여름엔 겨드랑이에 땀이 너무 많이 나요.
examples.romanization: yeoreumen gyeodeurangie ttami neomu mani nayo.
examples.en: My armpits sweat way too much in summer.
examples.note: 에(spot) + 땀이 나다 — Korea's humid summers make this daily

examples.en: I felt a lump in my armpit so I went to the hospital.
examples.note: real-situation health concern; 만져지다 = to be felt by touch

entries.nuance: 겨드랑이 is the armpit/underarm, a native Korean word with no everyday synonym — just memorize the ending -랑이. It is extremely practical in Korea's hot, humid summers for talking about sweat (땀이 나다) and odor; note that neutral 겨드랑이 냄새 is polite, while 암내 is a blunter, more loaded word for strong underarm B.O. that you should use cautiously. It also appears with 제모(除毛, hair removal), deodorant (데오드란트), and—seriously—with health checks, since a 멍울(lump) felt in the armpit can mean a swollen lymph node. The first English-speaker pitfall is spelling: people write 겨드랑or 겨드량이, but only 겨드랑이 is standard. The second is the sweat verb: 'I sweat' is 땀이 나다 (sweat comes out, sweat as subject), never 땀을 하다 — so 겨드랑이에 땀이 나요.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Misspelling it as 겨드랑 or 겨드량이 — the standard form is 겨드랑이.
Saying 땀을 하다 for 'to sweat' — it is 땀이 나다 (sweat as the subject): 겨드랑이에 땀이 나요.
Using the loaded word 암내 casually for any underarm smell — the neutral phrase is 겨드랑이 냄새.

entries.shortExplanation: 엉덩이 means "buttocks; hip area / bottom" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
entries.explanation: 엉덩이 (eongdeongi) = "buttocks; hip area / bottom". Treat it as a building block that needs a frame: 엉덩이가 아프다 ("for one's bottom to hurt") shows how it actually behaves. The grammar lives in the particle or ending beside 엉덩이, so notice that piece as you read, not just the dictionary meaning. Begin from a complete sentence about saying what hurts, asking for rest, and explaining basic health needs and swap just one element to make it yours.

usagePhrases.note: After long sitting; 이 marks the sore part

usagePhrases.en: to settle in and stick with it
usagePhrases.note: Idiom: 'plant your butt' = sit down and persevere

usagePhrases.en: to be slow to get going / a homebody
usagePhrases.note: 무겁다(heavy) used figuratively
운동 (運動, 'exercise'); common gym phrase

examples.en: My bottom hurts.
examples.note: Base sentence after long sitting

examples.ko: 딱딱한 의자에 오래 앉아 있었더니 엉덩이가 배겨요.
examples.romanization: ttakttakan uijae orae anja isseotdeoni eongdeongiga baegyeoyo.
examples.en: My bottom is sore from sitting on a hard chair too long.
examples.note: 배기다 = a hard surface presses into you — natural office complaint

examples.ko: 공부 잘하려면 엉덩이를 오래 붙이고 있어야 해요.
examples.romanization: gongbu jalharyeomyeon eongdeongireul orae buchigo isseoya haeyo.
examples.en: To study well you have to keep your butt in the chair a long time.
examples.note: 엉덩이를 붙이다 = to sit and persevere — a very common idiom

entries.nuance: 엉덩이 is the buttocks/bottom and the general seat-and-hip area. It is an everyday, non-vulgar word: fine in normal conversation, while 궁둥이 is the more childish/casual variant (often used with kids) and the clinical term 둔부(臀部) is hospital-only — default to 엉덩이. Keep it separate from 허리(waist/lower back): seat soreness is 엉덩이, but lower-back pain is 허리 아파요, and English 'I hurt my back/bottom' tempts learners to swap them. Idioms make this word punch above its weight: 엉덩이가 무겁다 ('heavy bottom') = slow to get up or a homebody, and 엉덩이를 붙이다 ('stick your butt down') = settle in and persevere at study or work. Collocations: 엉덩이가 배기다(sore from a hard seat), 엉덩이 운동(glute exercise). The pitfall is the idioms—don't read 엉덩이가 무겁다 as literal weight—and the 엉덩이 vs 허리 split for where it hurts.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Confusing 엉덩이(bottom/seat) with 허리(waist/lower back) — back pain is 허리 아파요, seat soreness is 엉덩이.
Reading 엉덩이가 무겁다 literally as physical weight — it is the idiom 'slow to move / homebody.'
Defaulting to 궁둥이 or 둔부 — 궁둥이 is childish and 둔부 is clinical; the normal word is 엉덩이.

structuredNuance.t: 엉덩이 is the buttocks/bottom and the general seat-and-hip area. It is an everyday, non-vulgar word: fine in normal conversation. Idioms make this word punch above its weight: 엉덩이가 무겁다 ('heavy bottom') = slow to get up or a homebody, and 엉덩이를 붙이다 ('stick your butt down') = settle in and persevere at study or work. Collocations: 엉덩이가 배기다(sore from a hard seat), 엉덩이 운동(glute exercise).

궁둥이 is the more childish/casual variant (often used with kids) and the clinical term 둔부(臀部) is hospital-only — default to 엉덩이. Keep it separate from 허리(waist/lower back): seat soreness is 엉덩이, but lower-back pain is 허리 아파요, and English 'I hurt my back/bottom' tempts learners to swap them.
The pitfall is the idioms—don't read 엉덩이가 무겁다 as literal weight—and the 엉덩이 vs 허리 split for where it hurts.

entries.shortExplanation: 구청 means "district (gu) office" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
entries.explanation: 구청 (gucheong) means "district (gu) office". Learn it inside a frame, not as a bare word: a useful first chunk is 구청에 가다 ("go to the district office"). In Korean the particle or ending next to 구청 signals its job — topic, subject, object, place, time, method, or description — so read the examples for the small piece beside it. Start with one real sentence about basic everyday communication, then change a single part.

usagePhrases.note: the destination always takes 에, never 에서, when you simply 'go there'

usagePhrases.en: get issued at the district office
usagePhrases.note: the place where an action happens takes 에서; for documents like 건축물대장 you go to 구청, a simple 등본 is fine at the 동사무소
민원실 is the help-desk floor where you take a 번호표 and wait at a 창구
관할 (管轄) is the office responsible for your registered address; it matters when filing complaints

examples.ko: 우리 동네 구청은 지하철역 바로 앞에 있어요.
examples.romanization: uri dongne gucheongeun jihacheoryeok baro ape isseoyo.
examples.en: Our neighborhood's district office is right in front of the subway station.
examples.note: simple location sentence; note 구청 takes the topic/subject naturally without a counter

examples.ko: 주차 단속 때문에 구청에 민원을 넣었어요.
examples.romanization: jucha dansok ttaemune gucheonge minwoneul neoeosseoyo.
examples.en: I filed a complaint with the district office about parking enforcement.
examples.note: 민원을 넣다 'put in a civil request' is the set collocation for lodging a complaint

examples.en: You register a business at the tax office, not the district office.
examples.note: real mix-up: 구청 handles residency and buildings, 세무서 handles taxes — '말고' means 'not X (but)'

entries.nuance: 구청 (區廳, 區 'district' + 廳 'government office') is the borough-level city government serving an entire 구, one tier above the neighborhood 동사무소 and one tier below the city-wide 시청. As a resident you go there for ID and property documents, building paperwork, and parking or noise 민원. The dividing line learners blur is 구청 vs 시청 vs 동사무소: 시청 governs the whole city, 구청 one district inside it, 동사무소 one small neighborhood — so for an everyday 등본 the nearest 동사무소 is enough and you rarely need the 구청. The 廳 ending specifically marks a large administrative seat, which is why a small front desk is a 민원실, not a 구청. A pitfall for English speakers is treating 구청 like a generic 'city hall'; the precise English is 'district/borough office', and you must say 구청에 가다 (에, the goal), not 구청에서 가다.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Confusing 구청 with 시청: 시청 (city hall) governs the whole city, 구청 governs just one district within it — saying 시청 for a district errand sends you to the wrong building.
Using 구청에서 가다 for 'go to the office'; the destination of 가다 takes 에 (구청에 가다). 에서 marks where an action is performed, e.g. 구청에서 서류를 떼다.
Going to 구청 for taxes; income and business taxes are handled at the 세무서, not the 구청.

structuredNuance.t: 구청 is the borough-level city government serving an entire 구, one tier above the neighborhood 동사무소 and one tier below the city-wide 시청. As a resident you go there for ID and property documents, building paperwork, and parking or noise 민원.

entries.shortExplanation: 동사무소 means "neighborhood community office (dong office)" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
entries.explanation: "neighborhood community office (dong office)" is 동사무소 (dongsamuso). The word itself is easy; what matters is the company it keeps, like 동사무소에 가다 ("go to the neighborhood office"). Watch the particle attached to 동사무소 in each example — that little marker, not the word, tells you whether it is the topic, the subject, the object, or a place. Copy one full sentence about basic everyday communication first, then vary one word.

usagePhrases.note: destination takes 에; 동사무소 is the smallest admin office, one per 동

usagePhrases.en: get (a document) issued at the dong office
usagePhrases.note: 떼다 'tear off / pull' is the everyday verb for getting a certificate like 주민등록등본; 발급받다 is its formal twin
가깝다 (ㅂ-irregular: 가까운, 가까워요) describes the closest branch most residents use
usually weekdays 9 to 6; 영업시간 or 업무시간, closed weekends

examples.ko: 등본 한 통만 떼러 동사무소에 잠깐 들렀어요.
examples.romanization: deungbon han tongman ttereo dongsamusoe jamkkan deulleosseoyo.
examples.en: I dropped by the dong office just to get one copy of my residence certificate.
examples.note: 통 is the counter for documents; 떼러 가다 'go in order to pull (a doc)' is the natural errand frame

examples.en: These days the dong office is officially called an administrative welfare center.
examples.note: the modern name is 행정복지센터, but everyone still says 동사무소 — N(이)라고 부르다 'call it N'

examples.en: When you move, file your move-in report at the dong office within 14 days.
examples.note: 전입신고 is legally required; late filing can mean a small fine

entries.nuance: 동사무소 (洞事務所, 洞 'neighborhood' + 事務 'administrative affairs' + 所 'office') is the neighborhood-level office where residents handle the commonest errands: 전입신고 (move-in reports), 주민등록등본/가족관계증명서, and ID paperwork. Its official name was renamed 주민센터 and then 행정복지센터, yet spoken Korean overwhelmingly keeps 동사무소 — a good lesson that the textbook term and the street term diverge. The contrast to nail is 동사무소 vs 구청: the 동사무소 covers one 동 (neighborhood) and is closer and faster, the 구청 covers the whole 구 and handles weightier property/building matters. The 所 ending (also in 보건소, 파출소) marks a modest local 'station/post', unlike the grand 廳 of 구청. Pitfall: English speakers say 발급하다 ('to issue', what the office does) when they mean 발급받다 ('to be issued / receive'); a citizen 등본을 발급받다, the office 발급하다.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Saying 동사무소 for the whole district; it only covers one 동 (neighborhood), not the entire 구 — for district-wide matters you need the 구청.
Mixing up 발급하다 vs 발급받다: you, the citizen, 등본을 발급받다 (receive it); the office 발급하다 (issues it). Using 발급하다 about yourself sounds like you run the office.
Assuming the self-service kiosk (무인발급기) is always free; a 등본 print is cheap or free, but you still must scan your ID to use it.
